summary.text: Space exploration is the physical investigation of outer space, by uncrewed robotic space probes and by human spaceflight.
It became possible only when large and relatively efficient rockets were built in the mid-twentieth century, and a Space Race between the Soviet Union and the United States drove the early era.
Later came renewable hardware like the Space Shuttle, cooperation through the International Space Station, and a rising private space industry.

facts.label: First orbiter
facts.value: Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957

facts.label: First human spaceflight
facts.value: Yuri Gagarin aboard Vostok 1, on 12 April 1961

facts.label: First crewed landing
facts.value: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969

facts.label: Space station
facts.value: The International Space Station was built between 1998 and 2011

facts.label: Confirmed exoplanets
facts.value: 5,284 had been discovered as of 1 December 2022

items.prompt: People have watched the sky since before written history, yet physically exploring space waited until the twentieth century. What changed?

options.label: Telescopes were invented
Large and relatively efficient rockets were developed
Astronomy became a recognised science
Governments stopped competing with one another

items.explain: Observing objects in space predates recorded history, but large efficient rockets in the mid-twentieth century made physical exploration real.

items.prompt: Sputnik 1 carried radio transmitters whose beeps were heard around the world. What did scientists learn by analysing the signals?

options.label: The composition of the Moon's surface
How fast Earth rotates
How strong the Sun's magnetic field is
The electron density of the ionosphere

items.explain: Analysis of the radio signals gathered information about the electron density of the ionosphere.

items.prompt: A rocket reaches 176 kilometers up, well above the Kármán line, yet falls back to Earth in an impact. What was missing?

options.label: Enough speed to reach orbital velocity
Enough height to cross the Kármán line
A crew to steer it back
A radio transmitter on board

items.explain: The rocket reached space but not orbital velocity, so it returned to Earth as a sub-orbital flight.

items.prompt: Luna 2 reached the Moon in 1959, but Luna 9 is credited with a different first in 1966. What was it?

options.label: The first artificial object to reach another celestial body
The first crewed landing on another celestial body
The first soft landing on another celestial body
The first artificial satellite of the Moon

items.explain: Luna 2 was the first artificial object to reach another body, Luna 9 made the first soft landing, and Luna 10 became the first satellite of the Moon.

items.prompt: In the 1970s, space agencies moved away from one-off flights. In what two ways did their focus change?

options.label: Toward private companies and away from governments
Toward crewed Moon landings and away from satellites
Toward renewable hardware and from competition to cooperation
Toward uncrewed probes and away from space stations

items.explain: The focus shifted from one-off flights to renewable hardware such as the Space Shuttle, and from competition to cooperation like the ISS.

items.prompt: Why did the Soviet Union and the United States pour resources into early spaceflight?

options.label: To demonstrate technological superiority over each other
To share costs on a joint orbital station
To find new planets to settle
To replace expensive telescopes with probes

items.explain: The early era was driven by a Space Race in which the two countries vied to demonstrate their technological superiority.
